exclusion_orientation: Review current NCCP exclusions, pregnancy, hypersensitivity, organ function and source-specific baseline criteria.
important_cautions: Doxorubicin hepatic decisions use absolute bilirubin in µmol/L, not an assumed ULN of 20.

LVEF < 50% is a baseline exclusion; the on-treatment discontinuation table uses < 45%.
The source’s > 20% reduction in baseline LVEF wording requires clinical definition; no automatic percentage-point conversion is encoded.
Dose levels: 75, 60, 50 mg/m², then discontinue; this is not repeated multiplication of the current dose.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Your team may choose a combination when reducing tumour size is an important goal and you are fit for more intensive treatment. For advanced disease, treatment generally aims at control and symptom relief; a combination is not a guarantee of longer survival.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care. Ifosfamide damages cancer-cell DNA. Its breakdown products can also affect the bladder, kidneys and brain. Mesna protects the bladder but does not prevent all kidney or brain effects.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 20 mg/m² and ifosfamide 3000 mg/m² on each of days 1–3, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Per-cycle totals are doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9000 mg/m². Mesna, hydration and other support continue for their prescribed periods.
key_points: This is NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9 g/m² per cycle. The two NCCP combination regimens have different doxorubicin doses and eligibility details. They must not be substituted for each other or for a published 10 g/m² ifosfamide regimen.

NCCP 00391: doxorubicin 20 mg/m² and ifosfamide 3000 mg/m² on each of days 1–3, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles. Per-cycle totals are doxorubicin 60 mg/m² and ifosfamide 9000 mg/m². Mesna, hydration and other support continue for their prescribed periods.

Blood count and kidney/liver tests before each cycle. Neurological assessment before every ifosfamide dose; check for blood in urine before each dose and every 8 hours on treatment days. Monitor fluid balance, urine output and electrolytes according to the individual plan.

Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential bladder protection. NCCP requires G-CSF support and proton-pump inhibitor prophylaxis for this regimen; the team specifies product, dose and timing. Multi-day anti-sickness treatment needs a single reconciled prescription. Aprepitant may increase ifosfamide-related brain toxicity, so pharmacy must check the chosen plan.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: In a first-line advanced soft tissue sarcoma trial, adding intensified ifosfamide increased tumour response and delayed progression, but did not demonstrate a statistically significant overall-survival advantage and caused substantially more toxicity. limitations: The trial used doxorubicin 75 mg/m² with ifosfamide 10 g/m² over four days. NCCP 00392 uses doxorubicin 75 mg/m² with ifosfamide 9 g/m² over three days. regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Dacarbazine may be used to control metastatic sarcoma and help symptoms. Expected benefit depends on tumour subtype, previous treatment and your overall condition; your consultant explains why this option is appropriate.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Dacarbazine is converted in the body into substances that damage DNA and make it harder for cancer cells to divide. It also affects some healthy cells, including blood-forming cells. This explains why nausea prevention and blood-count checks are central to the plan.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: NCCP 00511 gives dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² on day 1 every 21 days. The source describes 4 cycles or treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity; your consultant must specify the planned duration and review point.
key_points: This is dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² over 1 hour, not the 1 g/m² comparator used in some later trials. The current catalogue-linked NCCP document is version 2, reviewed March 2021 with a printed review-due date in March 2026; the treating team should confirm the current local protocol.

NCCP 00511 gives dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² on day 1 every 21 days. The source describes 4 cycles or treatment until progression or unacceptable toxicity; your consultant must specify the planned duration and review point.

Full blood count and kidney/liver tests before each treatment. Counts can fall several weeks after a dose, so report infection or bleeding even late in the cycle; symptoms or previous low counts may require extra tests.

This is a high nausea/vomiting-risk treatment. Follow the prescribed prevention, delayed-sickness and rescue plan, and contact the team if vomiting prevents drinking. Confirm any stomach protection and local mouth care. Avoid alcohol and have the team review potentially liver-toxic medicines and phenytoin.
